chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:

Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) descended to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) with two pomegranates from Paradise. He gave them both to him, so he ate one of them and split the other into two halves. He gave ʿAlī (عليه السلام) half of it, and he ate it. Then he said: “O ʿAlī, as for the first pomegranate that I ate, it is prophethood, and you have no share in it; and as for the other, it is knowledge, so you are my partner in it.”

key_terms.النُّبُوَّةُ: prophethood, reserved exclusively for the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله)
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the heavenly source of the two pomegranates
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: divinely granted knowledge shared by the Prophet with Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام)
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibrāʾīl, the angelic messenger who brought the heavenly gift
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, recipient of revelation and prophethood
key_terms.شَرِيكِي: my partner, indicating shared participation in knowledge

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Imam ʿAlī’s (عليه السلام) share in the Prophet’s knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith describes Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) bringing two pomegranates from Paradise to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), one representing prophethood and the other representing knowledge. The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) states that Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام) has no share in prophethood, but is his partner in knowledge, highlighting his unique rank in receiving the Prophet’s knowledge.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Azina, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘Jibraeel<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> descended unto Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> with two pomegranates from the Paradise. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> gave him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> these two. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> ate one and broke the other one into two halves, and gave Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> half of it, so he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> ate it, and he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘O Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>! As for the first pomegranate which I<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> ate, so it is the Prophet-hood, there isn’t a share for you in it. And as for the other, so it is the knowledge, so You<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> are my<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> associate in it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ‘Udhaynah from Zurarah from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Once Jibril brought from Paradise two pieces of pomegranate to the Messenger of Allah and brought him two pieces of pomegranates. The Messenger of Allah ate one of them and broke the other one into two pieces. He then ate one half and gave the other half to Ali (a.s.) who also ate it (a.s.). The Messenger of Allah said, “The first one that I ate was prophet-hood. There is no share in it for you. The other one is knowledge in which you are my partner.”
